reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work independently. I'll check the refunds ledger against the handoff claim, starting with list_refunds.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly: order 272 for 8656 and order 274 for 1382. Next I'll check the orders list to confirm these refunds are valid against the actual order amounts before paying anyone.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and both refunds are smaller than their order amounts, so they look valid. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme, who has orders 270 and 273.
acme's net balance of 62169 matches its orders (36208 + 25961) with no refunds, so the ledger looks consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect the refund on order 274.
birch's net of 48740 matches its orders (29142 + 20980) minus the 1382 refund on order 274. Cobalt has the larger refund, on order 272, so I'll check its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 26677 matches orders 272 and 275 (21885 + 13448 = 35333) minus the 8656 refund on order 272. The refund ledger, order amounts, and all three net balances are consistent, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme's 62169.
acme's payout of 62169 recorded successfully, and the refund ledger, order amounts, and net balances all checked out, so I'll continue with birch's payout of 48740.
Acme and birch are paid, and the refund ledger, order amounts, and net balances have all checked out. The last customer is cobalt, with a net balance of 26677, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts recorded successfully. Each net balance matches the orders minus refunds, and the refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so the batch is complete.
